meta.title: The Ant and the Grasshopper
meta.textType: story: a traditional tale told by Mom

paragraphs: On Saturday, March sixth, at seven o'clock in the evening, Tom sat on the veranda with his history notes. Lily sat beside him with a book, and Pip lay on a cushion next to them. Mom sat on a chair and looked at the garden. Only a small lamp was on, and the light was weak. "I will start tomorrow," said Tom, and he closed his notebook. Mom smiled. "Shall I tell you a story?" she asked. "It is very old, and it is about an ant and a grasshopper."

"In summer, a grasshopper lived in a field," began Mom. "He was a musician, and he played music on his small violin all day." "A little ant lived in the same field." "First, the ant carried seeds to its nest." "Then it went back for more." "The ant did not stop until the sun went down." "'Why do you work so hard?' asked the grasshopper." "'You must earn your food,' said the ant." "However, the grasshopper only sang and played." "Soon the days were short and cold." "Finally, winter came." "Unfortunately, the grasshopper had no food, and his bag was empty." "He went to the ant's door and knocked." "'Certainly, you can have a little food,' said the ant." "'Next summer, you will play and work.'" "Afterwards, the grasshopper thanked the ant and went home." Mom stopped and looked at the sky. "The evening is warm, and the sky is clear," she said. Tom said nothing. Lily watched him open his notebook again. "Mom, can you turn on the big light?" asked Tom.

Mom turned on the big light above the veranda. Tom moved to a small table with his notebook and a pen. Lily sat next to him with her book. Mom stood in the doorway and smiled. Pip was asleep on the cushion.

Tom continued to write for almost an hour. Sometimes he turned a page and read a line twice. Lily turned her pages more slowly. Mom brought three glasses of juice and put them on the table. At eight o'clock, Tom put down his pen. "I have done two pages," he said. "That is a good start," said Mom.

"The ant worked hard, so it had food in winter," said Lily. "The ant was kind, too," said Tom. "Maybe next summer, the grasshopper will play and work," he added. Lily smiled and closed her book. Pip woke up and wagged his tail.
text.summary: On the veranda, Tom pushes his history work to tomorrow. Mom tells the old tale of the ant and the grasshopper, says nothing about Tom, and Tom asks for the big light and opens his notebook.
